project: Brain Game — A Study in Cognition

regions.name: Prefrontal Cortex
regions.subtitle: Seat of Deliberation
regions.clickDescription: The prefrontal cortex orchestrates planning, decision-making, working memory, and the regulation of social conduct. It matures latest of all cortical territories and coordinates nearly every complex act of will.
regions.factoid: The Prefrontal Cortex, most expanded in humankind. The seat of deliberation and foresight.

regions.name: Orbitofrontal Cortex
regions.subtitle: Arbiter of Value
regions.clickDescription: Resting above the orbits of the eyes, the orbitofrontal cortex weighs reward and consequence, tempering impulse with expected value. Damage here famously alters temperament while sparing intellect.
regions.factoid: The Orbitofrontal Cortex, resting upon the orbits of the eyes. Arbiter of appetite and restraint.

regions.name: Premotor Cortex
regions.subtitle: Rehearsal of Movement
regions.clickDescription: The premotor cortex assembles the plan of a movement before it is executed, selecting and sequencing actions with guidance from the senses.
regions.factoid: The Premotor Cortex, where intended action is rehearsed before its performance.

regions.name: Supplementary Motor Area
regions.subtitle: Conductor of Sequences
regions.annotationLabel: Supplementary Motor Area — internally guided sequences
regions.clickDescription: The supplementary motor area coordinates sequences of movement generated from internal intention rather than external cue, including the coordination of the two hands.
regions.factoid: The Supplementary Motor Area, conductor of self-initiated sequences.

regions.name: Primary Motor Cortex
regions.subtitle: The Great Descending Command
regions.clickDescription: The primary motor cortex issues the final cortical command for voluntary movement, its territory mapped body part by body part along the precentral gyrus.
regions.factoid: The Primary Motor Cortex, from which the great descending commands of voluntary motion depart.

regions.name: Broca's Area
regions.subtitle: The Articulate Engine
regions.clickDescription: Broca's area assembles the motor program of speech and contributes to grammar and language production. In nearly all right-handed persons it resides in the left hemisphere.
regions.factoid: Broca's Area, named for Pierre Paul Broca, 1861. The seat of articulate speech.

regions.name: Primary Somatosensory Cortex
regions.subtitle: The Feeling Map
regions.annotationLabel: Primary Somatosensory Cortex — touch & body sense
regions.clickDescription: The primary somatosensory cortex receives touch, temperature, pain, and the sense of body position, arranged as a distorted map of the body along the postcentral gyrus.
regions.factoid: The Primary Somatosensory Cortex, whereon the body is drawn anew in feeling.

regions.name: Somatosensory Association Cortex
regions.subtitle: Interpreter of Touch
regions.annotationLabel: Somatosensory Association Cortex — integrating body sense
regions.clickDescription: This association territory interprets and integrates bodily sensation, allowing an object to be known by touch alone and the body to be located in space.
regions.factoid: The Somatosensory Association Cortex, interpreter of the language of touch.

regions.name: Angular Gyrus
regions.subtitle: Crossroads of Meaning
regions.annotationLabel: Angular Gyrus — reading, number & spatial meaning
regions.clickDescription: The angular gyrus stands at the crossroads of vision, hearing, and touch, serving reading, calculation, and the binding of words to meaning and space.
regions.factoid: The Angular Gyrus, crossroads where the senses trade their meanings.

regions.name: Precuneus
regions.subtitle: The Inward Eye
regions.clickDescription: Hidden on the medial surface, the precuneus serves visuospatial imagery, episodic memory retrieval, and reflection upon the self.
regions.factoid: The Precuneus, the inward eye of memory and imagination.

regions.name: Primary Auditory Cortex
regions.subtitle: The Listening Chamber
regions.clickDescription: The primary auditory cortex receives sound from the ears, arranged by pitch, and begins the analysis of rhythm, tone, and voice.
regions.factoid: The Primary Auditory Cortex, the listening chamber of the temporal lobe.

regions.name: Superior Temporal Gyrus
regions.subtitle: Hall of Voices
regions.annotationLabel: Superior Temporal Gyrus — voices & auditory scenes
regions.clickDescription: The superior temporal gyrus analyses complex sound, voices, and the melody of speech, and contributes to social perception.
regions.factoid: The Superior Temporal Gyrus, hall of voices and of melody.

regions.name: Wernicke's Area
regions.subtitle: The Comprehending Ear
regions.clickDescription: Wernicke's area serves the comprehension of spoken and written language, binding sound to sense. Like Broca's area it is strongly lateralized to the left hemisphere.
regions.factoid: Wernicke's Area, named for Carl Wernicke, 1874. Where heard words find their meaning.

regions.name: Inferior Temporal Cortex
regions.subtitle: Gallery of Forms
regions.annotationLabel: Inferior Temporal Cortex — object & face recognition
regions.clickDescription: The inferior temporal cortex recognises objects and faces, the terminus of the ventral visual stream, and traffics with memory in the naming of things seen.
regions.factoid: The Inferior Temporal Cortex, gallery wherein all seen forms are catalogued.

regions.name: Piriform Cortex
regions.subtitle: The Ancient Nose-Brain
regions.clickDescription: The piriform cortex, among the most ancient of cortical territories, receives the sense of smell directly, without the thalamic relay required of the other senses.
regions.factoid: The Piriform Cortex, the ancient seat of smell, older than memory itself.

regions.name: Cingulate Cortex
regions.subtitle: The Emotional Girdle
regions.clickDescription: The cingulate cortex girdles the corpus callosum, weaving emotion into attention, registering conflict and error, and lending feeling its urgency.
regions.factoid: The Cingulate Cortex, the girdle of emotion about the brain's great commissure.

regions.name: Primary Visual Cortex
regions.subtitle: The First Light
regions.clickDescription: The primary visual cortex receives the first cortical impression of sight, decomposing the world into edges, orientations, and contrasts before any object is known.
regions.factoid: The Primary Visual Cortex, where light first becomes vision.

regions.name: Visual Association Cortex
regions.subtitle: The Composing Eye
regions.annotationLabel: Visual Association Cortex — assembling the visual scene
regions.clickDescription: The visual association cortex composes edges and contrasts into colour, motion, depth, and finally the recognisable scene, in commerce with the parietal and temporal lobes.
regions.factoid: The Visual Association Cortex, wherein sight is composed into scenes.

regions.name: Cerebellum
regions.subtitle: The Little Brain, Vastly Peopled
regions.clickDescription: The cerebellum coordinates movement, balance, and motor learning, and holds the majority of the brain's neurons. Modern science finds it equally engaged in the timing of thought, language, and emotion.
regions.factoid: The Cerebellum, the little brain, containing more neurons than all the rest together.

regions.name: Brain Stem
regions.subtitle: The Stalk of Life
regions.annotationLabel: Brain Stem — vital rhythms & the great conduits
regions.clickDescription: The brain stem carries every fibre passing between brain and body and keeps the vital rhythms of breath, heartbeat, and wakefulness.
regions.factoid: The Brain Stem, the stalk of life, keeper of breath and heartbeat.
